about:
Twenty-three values of the nonlinearity parameter B/A of liquid metals, liquefied gases and two other substances, sea water and molten sulfur, under the three headings the table prints in its body, which are each row's group. The liquefied gases are measured far below 0 °C, and the page prints those temperatures with a minus sign, held here as negative degrees Celsius: liquid helium at −271.38 °C. Methane shows how strongly B/A depends on temperature in a liquefied gas, from 17.95 at −163.15 °C to 5.41 twenty-five degrees higher. Every value carries its reference in attributed_to.

The caption says "at atmospheric pressure", and six of the liquefied-gas rows cannot be: argon at −183.15 °C, methane at −153.15, −143.15 and −138.15 °C and nitrogen at −193.15 and −183.15 °C are above the gas's normal boiling point, and are liquid only under a pressure the page does not print. Their reference, [8.74], is titled a study of B/A in liquified gases "as a function of temperature and pressure". The six are served with a note saying so, hold no pressure, and the caption's condition is registered in docs/ERRATA.md.
